vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: HTTP Caching Fundamentals
vertices.description: Cache-Control headers, ETags, conditional requests, browser HTTP cache behavior.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Understood HTTP cache as middle layer between SW fetch() and CDN. Identified that fetch({ cache: 'reload' }) bypasses browser HTTP cache. Initially skipped this layer in pharmacology correction scenario but correctly integrated after prompting. Can trace full three-layer invalidation path.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Browser Request Lifecycle
vertices.description: Full request path: navigation → SW intercept → Cache API → HTTP cache → CDN → origin.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 2: Deepened understanding of server rendering sequence — server renders HTML shell (empty for 'use client' components), browser receives HTML + script tags, React hydrates, useEffect fires API calls. Connected this to standalone vs export insight: if server only produces empty shells, a pre-built static file does the same job. Correctly traced offline scenario: SW serves cached HTML shell, React boots, useEffect fires, SW intercepts API calls and serves from cache/queue.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Service Worker Lifecycle
vertices.description: Registration, installation, activation, update phases, waiting state, skipWaiting, scope rules.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Clean retrieval of all lifecycle phases. Understood activate as cleanup moment. Identified skipWaiting danger for mid-session users. Found first-install bug in ServiceWorkerRegistration (navigator.serviceWorker.controller check). Learned 24hr auto-check trigger.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Cache API & Storage Mechanics
vertices.description: Cache interface, cache versioning, storage quotas, eviction, IndexedDB for structured data.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Strong retrieval on cache-first safety (content-hashed URLs). Understood versioned cache naming pattern. Correctly identified single-cache anti-pattern. Designed multi-cache architecture by purpose.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Caching Strategy Selection
vertices.description: Choosing cache-first, network-first, stale-while-revalidate etc. per resource type.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Applied strategy selection in Serwist plan. SWR for study content, NetworkFirst for API, CacheFirst for static. Sized ExpirationPlugin entries. Correct route ordering.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Service Worker + CDN Cache Interaction
vertices.description: How SW caching composes with CDN edge caching. Double-cache problem, invalidation coordination.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Correctly identified SW network request hits CDN edge not origin. Understood cache purging vs TTL tradeoffs. Chose API-driven purge for StudyElf. Traced full invalidation sequence.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Service Worker + HTTP Cache Alignment
vertices.description: How SW fetch events interact with browser HTTP cache. Managing both layers consistently.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Learned fetch({ cache: 'reload' }) bypasses HTTP cache. Initially skipped this layer but integrated after prompting. Missed in first plan draft, caught immediately when prompted. Pattern internalized.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Web App Manifest & Installability
vertices.description: manifest.json for PWAs: name, icons, display modes, installability criteria.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Has manifest.json experience in non-PWA contexts (VM deployment, data bundles with checksums). Understands the concept of manifest as package metadata. No exposure to PWA-specific manifest fields or installability criteria.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: App Shell Architecture Pattern
vertices.description: Separating minimal UI shell from dynamic content for instant cached loads.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Guessed app shell was about enabling download for app-like OS behavior. Did not identify the UI skeleton + dynamic content separation concept. Fresh territory.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Offline Strategy Design
vertices.description: Deciding what offline capability an app needs: full offline-first, graceful degradation, or none.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Full three-layer invalidation trace. Designed multi-cache architecture by purpose. Production-ready Serwist caching config with correct strategies per resource type.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: WASM in PWA Context
vertices.description: How WASM modules interact with service workers, caching of .wasm files, offline compute use cases.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Asked good questions about WASM+PWA fit: whether it's a common pattern, data flow, caching gotchas. Drawn to client-side compute + privacy story. Has working WASM understanding but no PWA-specific WASM knowledge. Correctly intuited caching concerns exist.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Update Flow & Version Management
vertices.description: Designing update experience: detecting new SW versions, notification, skipWaiting/reload flow.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Understood skipWaiting danger. Designed user-controlled update flow with sonner toast. Found first-install bug. Correct versioned cache cleanup in activate.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: PWA Fitness Evaluation
vertices.description: The meta-skill: determine whether PWA is the right approach for a given application.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 2: Major architectural insight — discovered that standalone output mode provides no value for StudyElf since all pages are 'use client' with data loaded via useEffect. Server only produces empty HTML shells. Ran codebase analysis confirming zero Next.js server features used (no API routes, no middleware, no server actions, no SSR). Concluded static export eliminates unnecessary Node.js container (1 CPU, 1 GB) with zero feature loss.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Migration Path & Cost Assessment
vertices.description: Evaluating what it takes to move an existing application to PWA.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 2: Concrete standalone→export migration analysis. Ran automated codebase scan identifying only 2 trivial blockers (1 dynamic route, 4 missing Suspense wrappers). Mapped infrastructure changes (Dockerfile, docker-compose, Caddyfile). Identified CDN deployment options (Cloudflare Pages as natural fit given existing Cloudflare Tunnel). Understands NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL bake-time constraint requiring per-environment builds.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: PWA Anti-Pattern & Code Quality Detection
vertices.description: Recognizing common anti-patterns in PWA implementations, especially LLM-generated SW code.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Identified single-versioned-cache anti-pattern, stale tooling risk, skipWaiting anti-pattern, first-install prompt bug. Initially missed fetchOptions in own plan.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Workbox & PWA Tooling Landscape
vertices.description: Google's Workbox library, PWA Builder, Lighthouse audits. When to use Workbox vs raw SW code.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 3: Understood Serwist as declarative abstraction over raw SW. Caught next-pwa deprecation. Produced complete Serwist migration plan with correct @serwist/next vs @serwist/turbopack decision for static export.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Web Push Notification Architecture
vertices.description: Push API, Notification API, VAPID keys, server push pipeline, platform differences.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Guessed webhook pub/sub model — directionally useful but not the actual mechanism. No awareness of Push API, VAPID, or the SW-based notification pipeline.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Background Sync & Periodic Background Sync
vertices.description: Background Sync API for deferred actions, periodic sync, browser support limitations.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Session 2: Reinforced in retrieval probe (correctly recalled event sourcing sync model) and offline scenario exercise (correctly routed POST flashcard answer to IndexedDB queue). Understanding is solid at conceptual level but hasn't worked through implementation details like retry logic, conflict resolution edge cases, or Background Sync API registration.

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: PWA Performance Budgeting & Measurement
vertices.description: Setting and measuring performance budgets, Lighthouse, DevTools Application panel.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Not directly assessed on PWA-specific metrics. Strong general performance/cost/efficiency evaluation instinct from architecture background. Likely can reason about performance budgets once given the PWA-specific metrics vocabulary.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: Platform Constraints & Browser Differences
vertices.description: iOS limitations, Android capabilities, desktop PWA landscape, how constraints affect decisions.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Explicitly stated no familiarity with iOS/Safari PWA limitations. Guessed sandboxing requirements, which is reasonable but not the actual issue (storage eviction, limited APIs).

vertices.label: Skill
vertices.name: Server-Rendered (htmx) vs PWA Architectural Tension
vertices.description: Where htmx and PWA compose well vs conflict. Progressive enhancement strategies.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Correctly identified the core tension: htmx is server-side event driven, so offline breaks the model. Understands the htmx side well. Lacks the vocabulary of which PWA features compose well with htmx (manifest, basic SW = easy; full offline = fundamentally conflicts). Corrected the initial over-estimate of htmx expertise — uses it but it's not a deep strength area.

vertices.label: Concept
vertices.name: HTTPS & Service Worker Security Model
vertices.description: Why HTTPS is mandatory for SWs, SW as network proxy security implications, CSP considerations.

learner_state.evidence_summary: Strong TLS awareness — enforces TLS 1.3 on all projects. Understands encryption prevents 'all sorts of badness' and that browsers penalize HTTP. Doesn't yet know the specific SW-HTTPS requirement (browsers refuse to register SW on HTTP except localhost), but the security posture is already correct in practice.

transfer_leverage.scaffold_description: Your structured evaluation framework (intent, use-cases, lifecycle, reversibility, incremental rollout, opportunity cost) is directly applicable. We just need to populate it with PWA-specific decision criteria rather than building the framework from scratch.

Your migration assessment process (hit-to-implement, roadmap tradeoff, blockers, alternatives, worst case) transfers directly. We layer PWA-specific cost factors and htmx-specific migration paths on top.

Your structured code review pipeline (security, silent failures, type design, tests, simplification, codebase fit) is excellent. We add a PWA-specific review agent to the pipeline — same process, new checklist items.

You understand HTTP request/response from the server side. We flip the perspective to the client side — same headers, but now you're reasoning about how the browser acts on them rather than how the server sets them.

You understand the htmx side of the tension (server owns rendering, HTML over the wire). We fill in the PWA side so you can map which PWA features compose with htmx and which conflict. Recalibrated from near to moderate based on your correction about htmx depth.
Your TLS practices already satisfy the PWA requirement. Just one new fact: browsers refuse to register service workers on non-HTTPS origins (except localhost). Quick win.

gap_analysis.effective_scope_estimate: You're starting at roughly 13% weighted coverage, but your architecture evaluation and code review skills give you significant scaffolding for the highest-value components. The effective learning scope is about 65-70% of what a from-scratch learner would need. For the 8-hour sprint: realistic to cover the top 12-14 priority gaps to a familiar/proficient level, giving you a working decision framework. For the extended program: 3-4 weeks at 2-3 hours/week should bring the full graph to stable competence, with coached practice solidifying the evaluation and anti-pattern detection skills.
